title: Adaptive admin escalation, domain-affinity verification, and invite sanitization
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need to build an adaptive admin escalation and invite-sanitization subsystem that integrates with RBAC v2, the SSO/SAML onboarding flow, and audit logging. This ticket covers three coordinated areas: (1) domain-affinity verification and cross-tenant allowlist/denylist enforcement for org and team invites, (2) invite sanitization heuristics to detect suspicious email patterns and ephemeral addresses, and (3) adaptive escalation rules for org-admin actions (auto-block, notify security, require approval) driven by risk signals. The subsystem must produce rich audit events compatible with the existing observability pipeline and allow retrospective search by invite_token, domain, and escalation_decision.
acceptance_criteria: Domain verification: invites from unverified domains are flagged and optional org-level denylist/allowlist enforced
Invite sanitization: malformed, disposable, and high-entropy addresses are rejected or routed to approval based on policy
Escalation rules: risk scoring model (rate, domain reputation, SSO-mismatch, admin-tenure) triggers one of three outcomes: auto-allow, require-approval, auto-block
RBAC v2 integration: admin escalation decisions recorded as transient assertions in RBAC audit events and surfaced to Console activity feed
Audit logging: events emitted to kafka->datastore with fields: invite_id, email, domain_status, risk_score, decision, actor, timestamp
Canary rollout: changeable via Console feature-flag with circuit-breaker to roll back to previous invite policy behavior
E2E tests: deterministic test harness covering allowlist/denylist, SAML-provisioned users, and manual approval flows
updates: 2026-02-20 - Maya Chen: Created ticket. Draft risk model and initial set of signals (email entropy, domain age, MX record health, SSO binding status, recent invite rate).

2026-02-25 - Carlos Rivera: Spike complete. Prototyped email sanitizer using libdisposable and added domain reputation lookup via TrustScore API (POC). Performance impact measured: +1.5ms median latency on invite path in POC. Needs batching for domain checks.

2026-03-02 - Security review (notes): Require retention of raw invite audit events for 90 days, PII minimization in downstream logs, and KMS-encrypted storage for invite artifacts. Security team requested showback in Console for policy hits.
2026-03-05 - Design feedback (Ana Patel): UX for manual approval flow needs explicit tenant-scoped delegate role and one-click revoke in the pending-invites view. Added label 'design-needed'.

2026-03-09 - Carlos Rivera: Implemented audit event schema v2 draft (fields listed in acceptance criteria). Open PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1284. Needs review for backward compatibility with existing dashboards.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Integration test failures fixed for SAML-provisioned invited users where SAML NameID didn't match email; added a fallback check and audit flag 'saml_mismatch' before auto-blocking.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Latency on the invite path from synchronous domain reputation checks -> Mitigation: add local TTL cache and fallback to async enrichment with temporary 'pending' state
Risk: False positives blocking legitimate onboarding from new domains -> Mitigation: enable soft-failure mode (require-approval) with telemetry and manual override in Console
Risk: Audit trail growth and PII exposure -> Mitigation: redact email in long-term indices, keep invite_id and hashed_email for lookup, encrypt raw artifacts
Risk: RBAC v2 assertion churn from frequent escalation decisions -> Mitigation: emit aggregated decisions and TTL for transient assertions to avoid persistent policy noise
implementation_steps: Schema: finalize audit event schema v2 and update kafka producer contract
Backend: implement email sanitizer service with pluggable reputation adapters and caching layer
Auth: hook into SSO/SAML onboarding flow to surface saml_mismatch and enforce org allowlist when configured
RBAC: extend RBAC v2 assertion model to accept transient escalation_decision entries and add a cleanup worker
Console: add pending-invites view with manual approve/reject and policy hit details
E2E: add test matrix for SAML-bound invites, allowlist/denylist, and rate-limited invite floods
Rollout: feature-flagged canary with metrics: invite_accept_rate, manual-approve-rate, escalation_rate, median-invite-latency
test_plan: Unit: sanitizer heuristics and reputation adapter mocks
Integration: SAML flows with saml_mismatch, and RBAC assertion writes validated in staging
Load: simulate invite storms at 10k/min to ensure rate-limits and throttling behave
Security: pentest on invite endpoint and review of stored audit artifacts
notes: Prefer idempotent invite endpoints: all invite operations must be safe to retry. Use invite_token as idempotency key.
Consider later extension: tenant-scoped machine-learning model for invite fraud scoring if heuristics insufficient.
Coordinate with legal/compliance for retention and eDiscovery requirements for enterprise tenants.
